state: So my grandma used to make this banana bread every single Sunday when I was a kid, and I swear the whole house would smell like it from the second I woke up until we finally got to cut into it after lunch. I never wrote the recipe down while she was alive, which I regret, but a few years ago my aunt found a stained index card in grandma's recipe box and mailed me a photo of it, so now I'm passing it along the same way. You start by mashing four very ripe, almost-black bananas in a big bowl until they're basically liquid, then you beat in a stick of melted butter, three quarters of a cup of sugar, one egg, and a splash of vanilla. Once that's smooth, fold in a teaspoon of baking soda, a pinch of salt, and a cup and a half of flour, stirring just until the flour disappears, because overmixing makes it tough and dense. Pour the batter into a greased loaf pan and bake it in a 350 degree oven for fifty-five minutes, though grandma always said to start checking with a toothpick around minute fifty since every oven runs a little different. Let it cool in the pan for ten minutes before you turn it out, or it'll fall apart on you, trust me, I learned that the hard way at a family reunion and nearly cried in front of twelve relatives.
